input.justification:
The XPath query is built from the variable `bar`, which is assigned via a conditional expression: `bar = "This_should_always_happen" if 7 * 18 + num > 200 else param`. With `num = 106` fixed in the source code, the condition `7*18+num > 200` evaluates to `126+106=232 > 200`, which is always True. Therefore `bar` is always set to the constant string `"This_should_always_happen"` and never to `param` (the user-controlled value from `request.form.get(...)`). Consequently the XPath expression built in `query = f'/Employees/Employee[@emplid=\'{bar}\']'` never actually incorporates user input at runtime, despite CodeQL's taint tracking flagging the data-flow path from `request.form` to the `lxml.etree.XPath` sink. This is a classic OWASP Benchmark "always-true/false guard" pattern intended to test whether a static analyzer can reason about constant-folded conditions; since the condition is statically always true, the injection is not actually exploitable.</justification>
